samples.summary: Test comment claims Cmd/Ctrl+X is absorbed "without preventDefault" but nothing asserts it — the test dispatches the `cut` event manually regardless
samples.evidence: `the cut shortcut does not drop the image selection` (test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts:307-317) comments: "Cmd/Ctrl+X is absorbed by `imageKeyHandler` without `preventDefault`, so the native `cut` event still fires with the selection intact." The only assertion is `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).not.toBeNull()`. If `imageKeyHandler` (src/view/editor.ts:2298) were changed to call `e.preventDefault()` before returning true, a real browser would never fire the `cut` event and Cmd+X over an image would silently do nothing — but every cut test here would still pass, because `dispatchCut` fabricates the `cut` event itself. The keydown event is created with `cancelable: true` (line 94-96), so `expect(keydownEvent.defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` is available and would close the gap. Same applies to the copy variants at lines 217-226.

samples.summary: The fake clipboardData cannot detect a missing `preventDefault()` on the copy/cut event, the exact failure mode of issue #870
samples.evidence: `dispatchClipboard` (lines 74-87) stubs `clipboardData` with only `setData`/`getData`. `TextEditor.handleCopy`/`handleCut` (src/view/text-editor.ts:1195, 1228) must call `e.preventDefault()` on the image branch or the browser overwrites the clipboard with the (empty) textarea selection and nothing is written — the original #870 symptom. No test asserts `event.defaultPrevented`, even though the events are created `cancelable: true` (line 83), so the suite would stay green through that regression.

samples.summary: No test that undo restores an image removed by cut, despite the code documenting it as "one undo unit"
samples.evidence: `deleteSelectedImageInline` (src/view/editor.ts:2239-2252) calls `docStore.snapshot()` before `doc.deleteText`, and its comment says "Remove the selected image inline as one undo unit". The new cut tests (test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts:329-345) assert only that the inline is gone; no test undoes. Grepping packages/docs/test for `selectImageAt` shows copy-integrity.test.ts as the only consumer, and none of its cases call undo. If the snapshot were dropped, a cut image would be unrecoverable in the tab and the suite would not notice.

samples.summary: The cut describe block has no mirror of the copy test that text selection takes precedence over an image selection
samples.evidence: `handleCut` (src/view/text-editor.ts:1224-1232) duplicates rather than shares the `!this.selection.hasSelection()` precedence branch from `handleCopy`, so the copy-side test at lines 285-303 gives it no protection. If the cut precedence were inverted, a user cutting text would instead delete the selected image and leave the text in place — a silent, data-affecting mismatch. The `cutting a click-selected image` describe (lines 306-374) has no such case.

samples.summary: The `text/plain` flavour written for an image copy/cut is never asserted

finding.summary: The image cut path (Cmd/Ctrl+X on a click-selected image) has no test at all, despite being the only document-mutating branch added by this diff
finding.evidence: The diff adds a `cut` branch in `TextEditor.handleCut` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1224-1232) that writes the image to the clipboard and then invokes `imageDeleteHandler` → `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2243-2255), and adds `key === 'x'` absorption in `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:~2300). The new suite only ever dispatches `copy` (`dispatchCopy`, line 74) and only ever presses `'c'`/`'C'` (`pressCopyShortcut`, line 87). Grep for `handleCut|imageDeleteHandler|dispatchCut|'x'` across packages/docs/test returns nothing. If the removal, the clipboard write ordering, the undo snapshot, or the `x` key routing is wrong, a user loses an image with nothing on the clipboard and no test fails.

verdict.reason: The image cut path is tested. packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts has a dedicated `describe('cutting a click-selected image (issue #870)')` block (lines 306-373) built on a `dispatchClipboard(textarea, 'copy'|'cut')` helper (lines 74-90, with a `dispatchCut` alias at line 90). It covers: (a) `x`/`X` key routing through `imageKeyHandler` keeping the image selection alive (lines 307-327, matching editor.ts:2288-2300); (b) the document-mutating branch end to end (lines 329-345) — a real `cut` event is dispatched, the WAFFLEDOCS_MIME payload is asserted to carry the image inline (text-editor.ts:1229 -> writeImageToClipboard at 1261), and the doc is then asserted to have the image inline removed with text 'abcd' and `getSelectedImage()` null, which is the observable effect of imageDeleteHandler -> deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2242-2252, 2268); (c) a cut-then-paste round trip asserting exactly one surviving image (lines 347-373). The tests run the real `initialize()` editor against a MemDocStore with nothing relevant mocked, and the APIs used (selectImageAt/getSelectedImage/clearImageSelection) exist at editor.ts:317-321 and 3639-3652, so the coverage is real rather than vacuous. The reviewer's cited line numbers for the helpers do not match the working tree, indicating their greps hit a stale revision.

finding.summary: Test named 'an image selection is ignored when there is also a text selection' never selects an image, so it is vacuous coverage for the precedence it claims to test
finding.evidence: The test body (lines 279-291) calls only `editor._setSelectionForTest(...)`; it never calls `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2)`, so no image selection exists. The assertions (`text/plain === 'ab'`, `blocks[0].inlines[0].style.image` undefined) hold identically for a plain text copy with no image selection at all — i.e. they pass whether or not `handleCopy`'s text-selection-first precedence is correct. If the precedence were inverted (image branch preferred), this test would still pass while user copies of text over a selected image would silently write the image instead.

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing factual claim — that the test "never calls `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2)`, so no image selection exists" — is contradicted by the file. copy-integrity.test.ts:290 calls exactly `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2);`, and line 295 asserts `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).not.toBeNull()` before the copy is dispatched, enforcing the two-selections-at-once precondition rather than assuming it. The cited line range (279-291) does not match the test body either (the test spans 285-303; 279-283 are the preceding round-trip test). The precondition is genuine in the source: selectImageAt (editor.ts:3639-3646) sets `selectedImage` after clearing the text range, and _setSelectionForTest (editor.ts:3790-3796) only touches `selection`/`cursor` and never clears `selectedImage`, so both coexist. The assertions also discriminate the precedence: handleCopy (text-editor.ts:1188-1198) tests `!this.selection.hasSelection()` first and only then writes the image via writeImageToClipboard; under an inverted precedence the payload would be the single image inline, so `text/plain === 'ab'` (line 298), joined text `'ab'` (line 300), and `style.image` undefined (line 301) would all fail — compare line 251, where an image-only copy yields `style.image === IMAGE`. The test is therefore not vacuous coverage for the precedence it claims to test.
